source_paper.title: Prompt Tuning with Diffusion for Few-Shot Pre-trained Policy Generalization
source_paper.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) methods harness previous experiences to derive an optimal policy, forming the foundation for pre-trained large-scale models (PLMs). When encountering tasks not seen before, PLMs often utilize several expert trajectories as prompts to expedite their adaptation to new requirements. Though a range of prompt-tuning methods have been proposed to enhance the quality of prompts, these methods often face optimization restrictions due to prompt initialization, which can significantly constrain the exploration domain and potentially lead to suboptimal solutions. To eliminate the reliance on the initial prompt, we shift our perspective towards the generative model, framing the prompt-tuning process as a form of conditional generative modeling, where prompts are generated from random noise. Our innovation, the Prompt Diffuser, leverages a conditional diffusion model to produce prompts of exceptional quality. Central to our framework is the approach to trajectory reconstruction and the meticulous integration of downstream task guidance during the training phase. Further experimental results underscore the potency of the Prompt Diffuser as a robust and effective tool for the prompt-tuning process, demonstrating strong performance in the meta-RL tasks.

1. Prompt-Tuning Bandits: Enabling Few-S.explanation: This paper builds on the concept of prompt-tuning in offline RL, which is central to the source paper. While the source paper introduces the Prompt Diffuser for generating high-quality prompts via a diffusion model, this paper addresses the limitation of uniform sampling of prompts by proposing a bandit-based framework for adaptive prompt selection. The hypothesis in this paper is inspired by the source paper's focus on improving prompt quality and efficiency in offline RL, making it highly relevant.
